glosses: punctuality
punktualność
Exactitude à faire certaines choses dans un temps donné, comme on se l’est proposé, ou comme on l’a promis.

examples.text: Au marché et à la devanture du bureau des Postes, c’est avec une grande ponctualité et une assiduité jamais démentie que les ’'miskines’' et les alyatimes se donnent rendez-vous.

On pouvait subodorer que c’était mal barré pour l’équipe de Suisse quand une conférence de presse d’avant-tournoi, la semaine dernière, a commencé avec 35 minutes de retard. Pour le pays de la ponctualité, il s’agissait bien entendu d’un impair considérable.

examples.text: Its professed end [of logic], is to teach men to think, to judge, and to reason, with precision and accuracy.

examples.text: The jury doubted the accuracy of the witness' comments.

glosses: Attention to small details; accuracy.

examples.text: [W]hen making a passage from one feeding-ground to another, the sperm whales, guided by some infallible instinct—say, rather, secret intelligence from the Deity—mostly swim in veins, as they are called; continuing their way along a given ocean-line with such undeviating exactitude, that no ship ever sailed her course, by any chart, with one tithe of such marvellous precision.

glosses: Made, or characterized by accuracy.

examples.text: But there was nothing he could do about Villa's second when Agbonlahor crossed from the left and Bent finished with a precision volley.

glosses: The habit or characteristic of doing things without delay.
The habit of adhering to a designated time.

examples.text: You were punctual to your appointment: punctuality is the first of virtues, and a sign of pretty behaviour in a young man. I foresee that you will succeed!
